findings.reason: Confirmed. Route 1's brief lists the unit test 'A = Z_p: F-smooth, with Z/p(1) = μ_p'. Read as an identity in D((Spec Z_p)_et), and the brief gives no other reading, it equates Z/p(1) with the étale sheaf μ_p in degree 0. That is false. The paper's Example 1.5 (published p. 2; arXiv:2202.04818v2 p. 2, SHA-256 12eb19e4…0955, equal to the red team's) says Z/p^n(1)_X 'is the derived pushforward of µ_{p^n} from the fppf site to the étale site (or equivalently the fiber of p^n : G_m → G_m in the derived category of étale sheaves)'. Example 1.2 identifies it with the étale μ_{p^n} only over X[1/p]. Item /006 already states the derived formula. So H^1 is the étale cokernel sheaf of p on G_m. I checked the red team's stalk at the closed geometric point for p = 3. Let R be the strict henselization of Z_3, which is unramified with maximal ideal 3R and residue field F̄_3. If u³ = 4, reduction gives (ū − 1)³ = 0, so u = 1 + 3a and u³ ≡ 1 mod 9R. But 4 − 1 = 3 has valuation 1, so 4 is not a cube, and H^1 ≠ 0 there, while the étale μ_3 has no H^1. The fix is right: test Z/p(1) ≃ Rε_*μ_p ≃ fib(p : G_m → G_m), with H^0 = μ_p and H^1 = coker(p), and test the restriction to Spec Q_p separately.

Confirmed, with a sharper fix. Route 2's brief ends with the unit test 'the symbol {1 + pt, t} on the affine line over Z_p' and gives no domain. Bloch–Kato's symbols (§1.2, (4.3)) and Proposition 5.6 of the paper (published p. 23; arXiv v2 p. 24, 'generated by symbols from R … the image of R^× ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ R^×') need unit entries, as the red team says. The obstruction, however, is t alone. The sheaf M^q lives on the special fibre, and 1 + pt ≡ 1 mod p is a unit in every henselian local ring at a point of the special fibre. Its zero t = −1/p on the generic fibre has closure V(1 + pt) ≅ Spec Q_p, which misses the special fibre. The entry t vanishes along t = 0, which meets the special fibre at t̄ = 0, so the symbol is defined only over G_{m,F_p}. The right domain is U = Spec Z_p[t, t^{−1}] (or its p-henselization). Inverting 1 + pt as well, as the red team proposes, is harmless but unnecessary. The red team's check ρ_1(t dlog t) = ρ_1(dt) = {1 + pt, t} agrees with Bloch–Kato (4.3) for e = 1 and π = p. Severity medium is right: the defect is confined to one unit test.
